clue.text: Change a sponsor for the singers

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A choir swaps its financial backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges A SPONSOR into the eight letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sopranos are the highest-voiced singers in a choir, so the plural fits 'the singers'.

clue.text: Oh, say, can you see it's flying now!

definitions.text: Oh, say, can you see it's flying now!

parts.words: Oh, say, can you see it's flying now
parts.note: the opening words of the US national anthem, which asks whether the flag is still flying

explanation.surface: An excited shout drawing attention to something in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oh, say, can you see' opens The Star-Spangled Banner, the American anthem about the flag still flying.
explanation.definitionFit: The flag of the United States is nicknamed for its stars and stripes, and the anthem celebrates it flying.

clue.text: He's to cuddle Her Majesty

parts.note: to pet is to stroke or cuddle
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to embrace the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter is a man's name, so it stands for a male, 'he'.

clue.text: A quiet river location is suitable

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
the Po is the longest river in Italy
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A peaceful spot beside a river makes a fitting place.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means apt or well suited to the occasion.

clue.text: Bird left at bottom of river

indicators.note: in a down entry, at the bottom of means placed after the river word

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A bird has been abandoned on the riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at bottom of' puts L below OUSE, the name of several English rivers; 'left' reads like abandoned but is L.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is a thrush-family bird such as the ring ouzel.

clue.text: Mark on a black beetle

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone notices a blemish on a dark-coloured insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Hosts a meeting about locks

parts.note: c is circa, Latin for about
locks of hair are hairs

explanation.surface: Someone convenes a gathering on the subject of security locks.
explanation.walkthrough: C is circa, Latin for about; 'locks' suggests door locks but means tresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to preside over or host it; the verb matches 'Hosts'.

clue.text: Practises on slow cars

parts.note: re means on or about, as in business letters
hearses are funeral cars that drive slowly

explanation.surface: Someone trains using sluggish vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a performance beforehand; both are third-person verbs.

clue.text: Doctor researched globe for an exam

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor studies the world to prepare for a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is a verb rearranging RESEARCHED GLOBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A first university degree is gained by passing final examinations, so it loosely stands for an exam.

clue.text: Cry over value of a battle

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to sob is to cry
worth is value

explanation.surface: Weeping over how much a fight was worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SOB into BOS. Bosworth (1485) was the battle in which Richard III died.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosworth Field was the 1485 battle ending the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Turn to pint as a starter

indicators.note: turn tells us to twist the following letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker switches to a pint of beer to begin the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' rearranges the nine letters of TO PINT AS A; 'starter' looks like part of the drinking scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian course of cold meats and pickles served before the main meal, a starter.

clue.text: A medical man tours hospital for a specific purpose

indicators.note: tours means goes around, so the doctor's letters go round the hospital letter

parts.note: a doc is a doctor, a medical man
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A doctor does the rounds of a hospital with a particular aim.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used of something arranged just for one particular need, not generally.

clue.text: Arranges classes

explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to arrange them, and sorts are kinds or categories, as in all sorts.

clue.text: This type doesn't get a shift on!

definitions.text: This type doesn't get a shift on!

parts.words: This type doesn't get a shift on
parts.note: on a keyboard the shift key makes capitals, so typing without it gives small letters; 'get a shift on' also means hurry up

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a certain sort of person never hurries.
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters on a typewriter or keyboard are the ones typed without pressing the shift key.

clue.text: Worn out when retired

parts.note: read as 'worn when out, having retired': a garment put on when one has gone to bed and is out cold

explanation.surface: Something exhausted after its owner stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' looks like exhausted and 'retired' like stopped working; really it is clothing worn when one has retired to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose shirt is put on for sleeping, after one has retired for the night.

clue.text: Very tricky outcome when the opponents don't score

definitions.text: Very tricky outcome when the opponents don't score

parts.words: Very tricky outcome when the opponents don't score
parts.note: in bridge, taking every trick in a hand is the top contract, so 'tricky' is literal

explanation.surface: A difficult result in a match where the other side fails to score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very tricky' means having all the tricks in bridge, where winning all thirteen leaves opponents with none.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, winning all thirteen tricks of a deal is the top bid achieved.

clue.text: Rugby player follows senior teacher to the hold

indicators.note: follows means the rugby word comes after the teacher word

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school
a lock is a forward position in the rugby scrum

explanation.surface: A rugby forward comes after a head teacher into the ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hold' suggests the cargo space of a ship; it is a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlock is a wrestling grip around the opponent's head.

clue.text: City in Norway and Czechoslovakia

indicators.note: in signals the city lies within the letters of the following words, here inside Czechoslovakia

explanation.surface: A geography question lists places in Norway and the former Czechoslovakia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City in Norway' looks like the definition, but 'in' signals the hidden word, found inside czechOSLOvakia.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Norway is a city, which makes the surface sly.

clue.text: Henry's ship swaps parts for herb

indicators.note: swaps parts says the two halves of the ship's name change places

parts.note: the Mary Rose was Henry VIII's flagship

explanation.surface: A Tudor warship trades one section for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mary Rose was Henry VIII's warship; 'swaps parts' puts ROSE before MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic culinary herb.

clue.text: Photograph a card game

explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal photo, and also a children's card game where matching cards are called out.

clue.text: Places to wash in old city harbours

parts.note: Bath is an old English city in Somerset famous for its Roman baths
harbours as a verb means shelters or houses

explanation.surface: An ancient town's ports have spots for bathing.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a historic city in south-west England known for its Roman baths, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathhouses are buildings with baths for public washing.

clue.text: But is she a relative of the BBC?

definitions.text: But is she a relative of the BBC?

parts.words: But is she a relative of the BBC
parts.note: the BBC's affectionate nickname is a family term for a parent's sister

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman is related to a broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is Britain's national broadcaster, long nicknamed 'Auntie'.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is popularly called Auntie, and an auntie is a relative.

clue.text: Wine on Scotish island — and French fish

parts.note: red is wine, as in a glass of red
Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A drink on a Hebridean island accompanied by a French fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotish is misspelt as printed; MULL is a large island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Red mullet is a reddish sea fish prized in Mediterranean cooking.

clue.text: Get some rest on Galapagos island

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, here a stretch inside them

explanation.surface: A traveller takes a break on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across resT ON GAlapagos; the Galapagos suggest the island but are only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island kingdom.

clue.text: Follow compass points around the bend

indicators.note: around says the compass letters go round the bend's letter

parts.note: E, N, S and E are points of the compass
a U-bend is a bend shaped like U

explanation.surface: A hiker follows direction signs around a curve in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards as a result.

clue.text: She starts to slip under stool in eatery

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A woman begins to slide off a stool in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a woman's name, so it stands for a female, 'she'.

clue.text: Look in mine for the aviator

indicators.note: in places the looking word inside the mine word

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a mineshaft in search of an airman.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is the person who flies an aircraft, an aviator.

clue.text: Solicitor employed during an election

parts.note: solicitor looks like a lawyer but means one who solicits, here votes, door to door

explanation.surface: A lawyer is hired while voting takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here means one who solicits votes.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvasser goes door to door asking people for their votes during a campaign.

clue.text: Adder season

explanation.definitionFit: One who sums, an adder, is a summer, and summer is the warm season of the year.

clue.text: Need a gym to train for a heavenly body

indicators.note: to train means to put through exercises, so the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone requires a fitness centre for exercise to get a perfect physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to train' rearranges NEED A GYM; 'heavenly body' looks like a gym-honed physique but is a moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede is the largest moon of Jupiter, a celestial body.
